primary.title: The Quran
primary.author: Allah (revealed to Muhammad)
primary.rationale: The central religious text of Islam, believed by Muslims to be the literal word of God revealed to Muhammad. It is considered the most important primary source for understanding Muhammad's teachings and the early Islamic community.

primary.title: Hadith Collections (e.g., Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim)
primary.author: Various companions of Muhammad (compiled later)
primary.rationale: Collections of sayings, actions, and approvals of Muhammad. While compiled after his death, they are considered by Muslims to be authoritative accounts of his life and teachings, providing crucial biographical and theological information.

primary.title: The Constitution of Medina (Kitab al-Madinah)
primary.author: Muhammad
primary.rationale: A document outlining the relationship between Muhammad, the emigrants from Mecca, and the inhabitants of Medina, including Jews and other tribes. It is considered one of the earliest examples of a written constitution and a primary source for understanding early Islamic governance and interfaith relations.

secondary.title: Muhammad: A Biography
secondary.author: Maxime Rodinson
secondary.rationale: A seminal and comprehensive biography of Muhammad, offering a critical and historical analysis of his life and the context of early Islam. Though slightly before the 1976 cutoff, it remains a foundational scholarly work.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to the Quran
secondary.author: Michael Cook
secondary.rationale: A collection of essays by leading scholars that explores various aspects of the Quran, including its historical context, interpretation, and significance. It provides scholarly analysis relevant to understanding Muhammad's role.

secondary.title: Muhammad and the Origins of Islam
secondary.author: Fred M. Donner
secondary.rationale: A highly regarded scholarly work that examines the historical context and development of early Islam, focusing on Muhammad's role in shaping the new religious and political community.

suggestions.notes: Primary sources for Muhammad are primarily religious texts and early historical accounts that are often debated in terms of authenticity and interpretation by secular historians. The Quran and Hadith are central to Islamic tradition. Secondary sources are selected for their scholarly rigor and focus on historical analysis.
